newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Sixteen injured in bombings in northwest Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Sixteen injured in bombings in northwest Colombia.

text.p: At least 16 people were injured in bombings in northwestern Colombia on Tuesday and during the night, most of them in the city of Medellin, authorities said Wednesday.
Police spokesmen said the attacks included a blast outside the union offices of lingerie maker Leonisa that injured five people in central Medellin on Tuesday night.

A man lost half his left arm when he tried to remove a Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) flag booby-trapped with dynamite from a chain-link fence near Medellin's Universidad de Antioquia, police said. The FARC is the largest of Colombia's three leftist guerrilla groups.
Two houses were bombed in Medellin's Caicedo neighborhood during the night and five city buses were set ablaze.
The bombings and bus burnings followed an explosion Tuesday morning that injured 10 people outside the Medellin offices of Colombia's main banana growers association, AUGURA.
Two banana packing plants in the Uraba region of Antioquia province, of which Medellin is the capital, were destroyed by dynamite charges set by suspected FARC rebels.
